questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make chocolate at home
A new EU law that could make chocolate more expensive
Why dark chocolate is healthier than milk chocolate
The history of chocolate in Europe
questions.why: Becca says a new EU law could make chocolate more expensive, and they discuss its effects.

questions.q: What kind of chocolate do Neil and Becca like?
options: They both prefer milk chocolate to dark
Neil likes it with sea salt, Becca with chilli
Both love dark chocolate, with different flavours
Neither of them eats much chocolate at all
questions.why: Both love dark chocolate: Neil likes it with chilli, Becca prefers sea salt.

questions.q: What would the new EU law stop companies from doing?
options: Selling chocolate that contains a lot of sugar
Importing any cocoa from West Africa
Using plastic packaging for chocolate bars
Buying cocoa from recently cleared forest land
questions.why: Neil says it would stop them buying cocoa from land where trees were cut down in the last six years.

questions.q: Why does Albert Smith think the law won't change much for his business?
options: He knows exactly which farms his cocoa is from
His company is too small to be affected by it
He doesn't sell any of his chocolate in Europe
He grows all his own cocoa on his own farm
questions.why: He works with small co-op or social enterprise farms, and all his cocoa is traced back to the plantation.

questions.q: What challenge does Albert mention for some farmers?
options: They don't want to sell their cocoa to Europe
They can't grow enough cocoa in dry years
Remote farmers find it hard to give their location
They have to cut down more trees to grow cocoa
questions.why: He says providing geolocations is a challenge for very remote farmers, some without mobile phones.

questions.q: What might happen to chocolate lovers because of these changes?
options: They may have to pay even more for chocolate
They will find less choice in shops
Chocolate will become cheaper
They will have to buy chocolate online
questions.why: Becca says the price of chocolate might go up even more.

questions.q: Why is the first chocolate lover happy to pay more?
options: Because he earns a lot of money in his job
Because expensive chocolate always tastes better
Because he only buys chocolate as a gift
It helps local people and fights deforestation
questions.why: He says the money will give local people a better life and help tackle deforestation.

questions.q: What is the second chocolate lover's attitude?
options: He always checks where the cocoa comes from
He doesn't check and wants efficient production
He will stop eating chocolate if prices rise
He thinks chocolate is already too expensive
questions.why: He says 'absolutely not' to checking and wants production 'as efficient as possible'.
